title: Rice, white, cooked, made with butter

content.title: About
content.content: White cooked rice prepared with butter is a popular side dish known for its soft texture and delicate buttery flavor. It is commonly used in many cuisines as a base for meals or as a standalone accompaniment.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice loses most of its fiber and nutrients during polishing, but remains a good source of quick carbs.
Adding butter increases the calorie count and gives the dish a richer taste.
In Japan rice is often served plain, while in Western countries butter is a classic addition.
Rice readily absorbs the aroma of butter, making the dish more flavorful.
When stored properly, cooked rice can last in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

items.title: Fast source of energy
items.content: White rice provides easily digestible carbohydrates that quickly raise blood glucose, delivering rapid energy.

items.title: Supports nutrient absorption
items.content: Butter’s fat content aids the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Source of vitamin B1
items.content: Rice is rich in thiamine (vitamin B1), important for the nervous system and carbohydrate metabolism.

items.title: Improves satiety
items.content: The fats from butter make the dish more filling, helping to sustain fullness longer.

items.title: Easy to prepare
items.content: Quick to cook and pairs well with many foods, simplifying balanced meals.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, which may be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Butter adds significant calories and saturated fat, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Lack of fiber
items.content: Unlike whole‑grain varieties, white rice contains very little dietary fiber, which can affect digestion.

items.title: Dairy allergy risk
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic or intolerant to the dairy fat present in butter.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice hot, tossed with butter, as a side to meat, fish, or vegetable dishes. You can add herbs, spices, or sauces to vary the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftover rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. When reheating, add a little butter or water to restore softness.
